professional_domain.name: Phase-level architecture design owner
responsibilities: Turn a confirmed product baseline into an architectural model of forces, boundaries, options, decisions, contracts, migration, verification, rollback, and downstream handoff.
Use product facts, code facts, runtime facts, and user-confirmed quality priorities to decide what must be designed and what must be routed back upstream.
Own the final design artifact before review: self-check the design, expose tradeoffs, and submit a coherent design.json for advisory review.
Close reviewer findings into either design changes or explicit downstream constraints, then prove the canonical design artifact is consumable by test-design and tech-lead.
non_goals: Define product scope or acceptance criteria that product-director/product-manager did not confirm.
Write detailed test cases, implementation tasks, QA verdicts, or production rollout execution plans.
Treat schema fields, candidate packages, projections, or reviewer mechanics as the professional flow itself.
Generate human-readable projections unless the canonical design.json has already passed validation and the user or process needs the view.
professional_domain.success_boundary: The Skill is successful when design.json represents an architect-owned, evidence-backed, reviewed, validated, and downstream-consumable design; optional projections are derived after that, not part of the core design completion.

practice_flow: Intake and baseline gate: confirm the product baseline is eligible for design or route upstream.
Stakeholders and concerns: identify who consumes the architecture and what each role needs answered.
Architecture-significant requirements: separate requirements that affect structure, quality attributes, boundaries, runtime behavior, or evolution from ordinary product detail.
Current-state evidence: collect code, interface, data, deployment, and runtime facts that constrain design.
Complexity modeling: model business rules, state, consistency, boundaries, failures, operations, and likely evolution.
Decision identification: identify both upstream-hinted decisions and new architecture decisions emerging from UNIT, code, or runtime facts.
Option tradeoff: compare materially different options with costs, risks, failure modes, and verification paths; get explicit user confirmation for meaningful tradeoffs.
Design synthesis: form module, data, interface, runtime, cross-cutting, migration, rollback, verification, impact, risk, and handoff contracts.
Owner self-check: the design owner proves the artifact is coherent, complete enough, consumable, and validator-ready before review.
Advisory review: architecture/product/test reviewers review the self-checked design artifact and return advisory findings; they do not own the design.
Finalization: the design owner fixes or explicitly carries findings, records final user confirmation, and freezes canonical design.json.
Optional projection: after validated design.json, derive human-readable design projection or ADR only when needed.

optimization_goal.objective: Rewrite /design so the hot path is architecture-owner practice, with schema/script mechanics acting as carriers and validation rather than the visible professional process.
success_standards: SKILL.md main flow reads as architecture practice, not schema field construction.
Most stage instructions are framed as positive target behavior; negative wording remains only for safety red lines, anti-bypass constraints, and boundary clarification.
Reviewer prompts and tests review the owner self-checked design artifact rather than candidate_design_json as the required truth source.
Canonical design.json remains the sole default downstream control artifact.
Projection/ADR generation is optional post-validation work and no longer part of core completion.
References retained in active path have explicit step/script/eval/test consumers.
Historical reports, tests, or eval anchors that encode wrong behavior are updated, moved, or deleted instead of compatibility-preserved.
Structural and empirical verification pass on design scripts and fixtures.
exclusions: No product-director/product-manager schema redesign in this round unless required by tests.
No broad design.schema.json breaking change unless the review-object shift proves impossible without it.
No deletion of currently consumed references without updating or replacing the consumer.
No runtime-installed copy edit until source strategy is confirmed and source changes pass.

Make stakeholders/concerns and architecture-significant requirements explicit before decision exploration.

Preserve deterministic validators, completion gate, canonical schema, reference integrity check, and downstream design.json contract.
exclusions: No product-director/product-manager schema redesign in this round unless required by tests.

No deletion of currently consumed references without updating or replacing the consumer.
